title: Telomere maintenance without increasing cancer risk
bottleneck: Telomere shortening limits cell division and drives senescence, but activating telomerase to extend telomeres is intrinsically oncogenic: most cancers reactivate telomerase to become immortal. Transient or tissue-specific telomerase activation extended mouse healthspan in studies, yet the safe therapeutic window in humans is unknown.
why_it_blocks: Telomere attrition is one of the few aging mechanisms with a clean molecular target, but the cancer tradeoff has frozen it as a therapy. Solving the safety problem would unlock a direct lever on cellular aging.
current_state: Small-molecule telomerase activators (e.g., TA-65/cycloastragenol) are sold as supplements with weak evidence. Gene-therapy telomerase approaches exist only in animal studies; no clinical program has cleared the cancer-risk question. Transient telomerase mRNA delivery extended healthspan in mice without raising tumor incidence in short studies, but long-term cancer surveillance data in any mammal are entirely absent.
